三、旅圖之間，隔壁家的那一天: 3. Between the journeys: one day at the house next door
下一次聽到陌生聲音時，你也許會停一下。想想它從哪裡來。想想是氣、弦、皮膜、木頭、: The next time you hear an unfamiliar sound, you may pause. Think about where it comes from. Think whether it is air, a string, a skin, wood, metal, a key — or a gesture someone left behind long ago.
也帶上一點手邊的小東西吧。薄紙、橡皮筋、紙盒、鉛筆、鑰匙、湯匙、杯子，都可能在某: Bring a few small things from around you as well. Thin paper, a rubber band, a paper box, a pencil, a key, a spoon, a cup — any of them may suddenly be useful on some page. They cannot speak for the real instruments, but they will open a small window for the ears first.
二、桌上的地圖慢慢亮起來: 2. The map on the table slowly lights up
五、古老的聲音，今天的耳朵，手邊的小實驗: 5. Old sounds, today's ears, small experiments at hand
傍晚來得很慢。桌上的弦還沒收完，房間的光已經被拉長。女孩本來還在比較琴身，聽到一: Evening comes slowly. The strings on the table are not put away yet, and the light in the room has already been drawn long. The girl was still comparing the bodies of instruments; then she hears a stretch of bowing and her pen stops on the page. The boy does not speak at once either. Through this passage everyone talks a little more quietly, as if afraid of breaking that long tone.
傍晚，光被拉長，弦也被拉長。豎琴、里拉琴、科拉琴、克拉爾琴，讓開放弦像天空和河流: In the evening the light is drawn long, and so are the strings. The harp, the lyre, the kora and the krar let open strings cycle like sky and river. The erhu, the morin khuur, the sarangi, the kamancheh, the rebab and the hurdy-gurdy let bow hair draw the sound into crying and singing.
先不急著談第一件樂器。第 001 篇，是隔壁家的第一個早晨。水壺、杯子、植物、地: No rush to talk about the first instrument. Piece 001 is the first morning at the house next door. The kettle, the cup, the plant, the rug, the record player, the small movements of the pets — they wake the ears first.
六、出發前，請帶上這幾樣東西: 6. Before you set out, bring these things
再往外走，聲音進入廣場。甘美朗合奏、阿拉伯塔赫特合奏、安地斯合奏、墨西哥流浪樂隊: Further out, the sound reaches the square. Gamelan ensembles, the Arab takht, Andean ensembles, mariachi, bluegrass bands, West African drum ensembles, Chinese orchestras, symphony orchestras, jazz big bands and modern mixed line-ups let us hear how many voices divide the work, answer each other, wait and hold each other up.
再靠近一點，姆比拉、卡林巴、手碟、空靈鼓、頌缽、音樂盒，把聲音縮到手心與耳邊。它: Closer still, the mbira, the kalimba, the handpan, the tongue drum, the singing bowl and the music box shrink the sound down to the palm and the ear. They are not necessarily loud, but they leave light in the room. The chinchilla brings everyone a little closer, and the capybara reminds everyone not to hurry on to the next passage.
到了午後，風慢慢停下來。女孩把吹管樂器的照片收進一疊資料夾，又從旁邊抽出另一疊：: By afternoon the wind slowly stops. The girl puts the wind-instrument photographs back into one folder and pulls out another: round-backed lutes, long-necked lutes, zithers, bridges, tuning pegs, soundboxes. The sunlight falls slanting across the table as if it too had become a string. The boy listens to the plucking — one, one, one — and says suddenly: “It sounds like someone walking along and singing.”
刺蝟的兩下暗號：拿兩支鉛筆輕敲，試著敲出「等一下」「走吧」「停在這裡」三種感覺。: The hedgehog's two-tap signal: tap two pencils lightly and try to make three feelings — “wait”, “let's go”, “stop here”. Short sounds have expressions too.
午後，桌上換成木頭與弦。烏德琴、魯特琴、琵琶、三味線、錫塔琴、曼陀林、斑鳩琴，像: In the afternoon the table changes to wood and strings. The oud, the lute, the pipa, the shamisen, the sitar, the mandolin and the banjo hold their stories the way a traveller holds them against the chest. Pluck, and the sound lights up; it lights up and is gone again, like a footstep, like a sentence not yet finished.
古老的聲音，藏在材料、地理、社群、儀式、勞動、節慶、宮廷、街頭、身體手勢與傳承裡: Old sounds are held in materials, geography, communities, rituals, work, festivals, courts, streets, gestures of the body and what is passed down. Today's ears meet them again through recordings, exhibitions, films, databases, live performance, sampling, soundtracks and new work.
可以一起做：閉上眼睛一分鐘，找出房間裡三個很小的聲音。水壺、冷氣、窗簾、衣服摩擦: Try it together: close your eyes for a minute and find three very small sounds in the room. The kettle, the air conditioner, the curtain, clothes rubbing, your own breathing — they all count.
可是耳朵已經不一樣了。: But the ears are different now.
四、六段旅圖，六種靠近世界的方式: 4. Six journeys, six ways of coming closer to the world
在世界出發以前，耳朵先在隔壁家醒來: Before setting out into the world, the ear wakes up at the house next door
夜再深一點，刺蝟反而精神很好。桌上出現木棒、鑰匙、鈴、石頭、杯子、小沙鈴。房間變: Later at night the hedgehog is wide awake. Wooden sticks, keys, bells, stones, cups and small shakers appear on the table. The room becomes a city of echo: on one side, streets laid out in wood, stone and metal; on the other, stardust of rhythm falling in the palm.
夜裡開燈，地毯先聽見低音。金貝鼓、塔布拉鼓、木箱鼓、達布卡鼓、太鼓，讓鼓面中心、: The lamp goes on at night and the rug hears the low end first. The djembe, the tabla, the cajón, the darbuka and the taiko make the centre of the drumhead, its edge, the palm, the fingertips, the mallet and the weight of the body all part of the sound.
夜裡，燈打開了。地毯、木桌、杯子、腳步，都開始像會回答人。男孩先被鼓聲帶走，肩膀: At night the lamp goes on. The rug, the wooden table, the cups, the footsteps all begin to seem as if they answer. The boy is carried off by the drums first, shoulders swaying gently. The girl taps the middle of the tabletop, then the edge, and finds the sound really is different. A cardboard box can teach a little about hollow space; the rim of a cup can teach a little about the tail of a sound. The capybara settles lower, as if reminding everyone: don't hurry, the sound is still in the room.
女孩把照片分成好幾疊。吹管放在窗邊，弦樂器靠近木桌，鼓和小打擊先暫時排在地毯上。: The girl sorted the photographs into several piles. Wind instruments by the window, strings closer to the wooden table, drums and small percussion laid out on the rug for now. The boy opened a playlist, and before the first track had finished the capybara had already set its chin back on the floor, as if ready to sit with everyone and wait all day for the last of the sound.
女孩會研究吹口、指孔、簧片和號角形狀；男孩會聽長音怎麼穿過胸口。白兔注意換氣聲，: The girl studies mouthpieces, finger holes, reeds and the shape of horns; the boy listens to how a long tone passes through the chest. The white rabbit notices the sound of breathing, the capybara waits for the tail of the sound, the hedgehog watches the small signal inside the jaw harp.
女孩本來想繼續看構造，聽著聽著，筆卻停在紙上。男孩本來沉在聲音裡，聽久了，也回頭: The girl had meant to go on reading about how it was built; but as she listened, her pen stopped on the page. The boy had been sunk in the sound; after a while he turned and asked: “Why does it ring like that?”
她把一張陌生樂器的照片推到桌邊，眼睛亮得像剛打開一個寶箱。孔在哪裡？弦怎麼排？那: She pushed a photograph of an unfamiliar instrument to the edge of the table, eyes bright as if she had just opened a treasure chest. Where are the holes? How are the strings laid out? That round soundbox — whose voice is it helping? Two instruments that look almost the same: how can their sound differ so much?
它從水壺快滾以前，那一點細細的顫開始。從杯子碰到木桌，短短一聲開始。從窗邊植物被: It begins with the thin tremble of a kettle just before it boils. With the short sound of a cup meeting a wooden table. With the wind reaching the plant by the window, a leaf brushing the wall. With the small patch of quiet in the room before the record player has started to turn.
帶上一點好奇心。女孩會帶你看孔洞、弦數、材料、形狀和小小差異。: Bring a little curiosity. The girl will show you holes, numbers of strings, materials, shapes and small differences.
帶上一點安靜。男孩會提醒你，有些聲音要先讓它落到身體裡，才知道它厲害在哪裡。: Bring a little quiet. The boy will remind you that some sounds have to fall into the body first before you know what is strong about them.
帶上一點時間。水豚會等尾音，白兔會注意小聲，刺蝟會抓住短音，絨鼠會讓大家靠近。: Bring a little time. The capybara waits for the tail of a sound, the white rabbit notices what is quiet, the hedgehog catches the short sounds, the chinchilla brings everyone closer.
手邊的小實驗，讓身體先靠近一點。吹紙不等於奈伊笛，橡皮筋也不等於科拉琴；紙箱只能: The small experiments at hand let the body come a little closer first. Blowing on paper is not a ney, and a rubber band is not a kora; a cardboard box only lends us a little hollow space, and a pencil only lends us the feel of how a short sound lines up with time. The real instruments, the players and the cultural context still have to be learned properly.
掌心裡還有星塵。沙鈴、謝克雷、卡巴薩、刮瓜、克拉維斯、響板、雨聲棒、鈴串、三角鐵: There is stardust in the palm as well. Shakers, shekere, cabasa, guiro, claves, castanets, rain stick, string of bells, triangle: the sounds are short, bright and exact, like small signposts set down in the music. The hedgehog is especially busy here, because it cannot miss a single short sound.
接著，氣會碰到簧片。口簧琴、笙、葫蘆絲、杜讀管、祖爾納管、風笛，把一小片會震動的: Then the air meets a reed. The jaw harp, the sheng, the hulusi, the duduk, the zurna and the bagpipes turn one small vibrating piece into a nasal tone, a singing voice, a procession, a wail, a whisper at the ear. Further on, lips vibrating carry the sound further still: the animal horn, the conch, the alphorn and the dungchen, as if waking a mountain, a sea or a crowd of people.
於是，他們把耳機分成兩邊。一邊是資料，一邊是感受。一邊看見細節，一邊讓聲音落進身: So they split the headphones in two. On one side information, on the other feeling. One side sees the details, the other lets the sound fall into the body. Put the two sides together and it is just like a door.
旅圖門口｜耳朵，可以醒來了: Journey entrance | The ears can wake up now
早晨開窗時，風先進來。紙角被吹動，女孩拿起一張薄紙，往邊緣輕輕吹，紙巾抖了一下。: In the morning the window opens and the wind comes in first. The corner of a page lifts; the girl picks up a sheet of thin paper, blows gently across the edge, and the tissue shivers. The white rabbit turns its head at once. At that moment no one has actually held a ney, a shakuhachi or a bansuri yet, but they already understand a little: air does not pass through empty — it meets an edge, it gets split, it makes something tremble.

最後，桌邊多了一台鍵盤和一台電腦。老照片、取樣片段、網站資料庫、博物館示範影片，: At the end a keyboard and a computer join them at the table. Old photographs, sample clips, website databases and museum demonstration videos are spread out together. The sound may come from the wind of an organ, from the bellows of an accordion, from tape, circuits, samplers and synthesizers — or from a square where many people play at once. Old sounds begin to reach today's ears.
最後，鍵盤與電腦打開。管風琴、簧風琴、手風琴、班多鈕手風琴、鋼片琴、電鋼琴、美樂: At last the keyboard and the computer open up. The organ, the harmonium, the accordion, the bandoneon, the celesta, the electric piano, the Mellotron, synthesizers, samplers, drum machines and the theremin bring keys, bellows, hammers, tape, circuits and control signals in together.
有些弦平放在大地上。古箏、古琴、日本箏、伽倻琴、卡農琴、揚琴、桑圖爾琴、鋼琴，讓: Some strings lie flat on the ground. The guzheng, the guqin, the koto, the gayageum, the kanun, the yangqin, the santur and the piano let fingers, hammers, bridges and soundboxes speak together. The girl compares short necks and long necks, round backs and flat backs, numbers of strings and bodies; the boy listens to how a plucked note lingers in the wood.
有些聲音已經換了新的路。它們進入博物館、錄音、影片、採樣音源、影視配樂或現代舞台: Some sounds have taken new roads. They enter museums, recordings, films, sample libraries, soundtracks or modern stages; they may also come quietly closer through headphones, records, web pages, theatres — or even through a sheet of paper, a paper box or two pencils on the table.
有些聲音從山谷、河邊、沙漠、島嶼、寺院、宮廷、街頭或祭典裡來。它們帶著材料的氣味: Some sounds come from valleys, riverbanks, deserts, islands, monasteries, courts, streets or festivals. They carry the smell of their materials, the trace of a gesture, the memory of a community, and the wind, light, footsteps and way of speaking that only certain places have.
樹葉、紙巾、橡皮筋、紙箱、湯匙、鑰匙和鉛筆，當然不是那些真正的樂器。它們只是小小: Leaves, tissues, rubber bands, cardboard boxes, spoons, keys and pencils are of course not the real instruments. They are only small entrances. Thin paper lets you feel how airflow makes something tremble; a cardboard box lets the palm learn that the centre, the edge and the hollow space are different; two pencils let a short sound stand steady on the tabletop for a moment.
每一疊照片都在問同幾件事：這個聲音從哪裡來？它靠什麼方式響起來？今天還能在哪裡遇: Every pile of photographs asked the same few questions. Where does this sound come from? What is it that makes it ring? Where can you still meet it today?
水壺還是那個水壺，杯子還是那個杯子，植物還在窗邊，白兔還會被小聲音吸引，刺蝟還會: The kettle is still that kettle, the cup is still that cup, the plant is still by the window, the white rabbit is still drawn to small sounds, the hedgehog still fixes on that signal, the capybara is still waiting for the tail of the sound, the chinchilla still brings everyone a little closer.
水豚說：等尾音一下。用手指輕彈一條橡皮筋，或輕碰杯緣，聲音出現後先不要說話，等它: The capybara says: wait for the tail of the sound. Flick a rubber band with a finger, or touch the rim of a cup, and once the sound appears, do not speak. Wait until it has really gone.
深夜，房間變成回聲城市。甘美朗、鑼群、編鐘、編磬、木琴、巴拉風、馬林巴、安克隆竹: Late at night the room becomes a city of echo. Gamelan, gong ensembles, bronze chimes, stone chimes, the xylophone, the balafon, the marimba and the angklung lay wood, stone, metal and bamboo out into a city that rings. Every sound has its place; they leave gaps for each other and light each other up.
清晨，水壺還沒滾，耳朵先醒來。女孩把筆記本打開，男孩把耳機分一邊，白兔從地毯邊緣: At dawn, before the kettle boils, the ears wake first. The girl opens her notebook, the boy takes one side of the headphones, the white rabbit crosses the edge of the rug, the hedgehog looks up, the capybara is still waiting for the cup's ring to die away. The world has not set out yet, and the room has already begun to ring.
男孩的閉眼小實驗：把橡皮筋套在空紙盒上，輕輕撥一下，再換不同大小的盒子。聽聽音高: The boy's eyes-closed experiment: stretch a rubber band over an empty cardboard box, pluck it gently, then try boxes of different sizes. Listen for whether the pitch, the brightness and the tail of the sound change.
白兔的資料小探險：聽到一段陌生樂器聲時，試著查三件事：它原本在哪裡響？誰演奏它？: The white rabbit's small research expedition: when you hear an unfamiliar instrument, try to find out three things. Where did it originally sound? Who plays it? Where can you still hear it today?
窗戶打開，第一段旅圖從一口氣開始。奈伊笛、尺八、簫、班蘇里笛、克納笛、排簫、陶笛: The window opens and the first journey begins with one breath. The ney, the shakuhachi, the xiao, the bansuri, the kena, the panpipes, the ocarina and the didgeridoo let us hear airflow, the mouth of a pipe, an edge, a long tone, and the space inside the body.
絨鼠邀你靠近一點：用指尖輕敲紙箱中央與邊緣，再用湯匙輕碰杯緣。先聽「哪裡發聲」，: The chinchilla invites you closer: tap the middle and the edge of a cardboard box with a fingertip, then touch the rim of a cup with a spoon. First listen for where the sound starts, then for where it stops.
讀到這裡，其實行李已經差不多了。耳朵帶上，好奇心帶上，手指、胸口、腳底也一起帶上: By this point the luggage is nearly packed. Bring your ears, bring your curiosity, and bring your fingers, your chest and the soles of your feet as well. The first road on the map is lighting up by the window.
跟女孩一起試試這個小機關吧：拿一張薄紙或紙巾，對著邊緣輕輕吹，觀察它怎麼震。不要: Try this little mechanism with the girl: take a sheet of thin paper or a tissue, blow gently across the edge, and watch how it trembles. Do not breathe it into your mouth, and do not use anything dirty or too small.
這一段不急。女孩也許本來還想追問構造，聽著聽著，筆停下來。男孩會把播放倒回去，因: There is no hurry in this passage. The girl may have wanted to ask more about how it is built; as she listens, the pen stops. The boy rewinds the track, because some drawn-out sounds you hear only once, and the heart is not ready to let go.
這一站像把鞋帶繫好。聲音不一定要很宏大才值得聽。只要願意停一下，世界在家裡就已經: This stop is like tying your shoelaces. A sound does not have to be grand to be worth hearing. If you are willing to stop for a moment, the world is already ringing inside the house.
這一站會把古老的聲音交給今天的耳朵。錄音、博物館示範、復原演奏、影視配樂、劇場軟: This stop hands old sounds over to today's ears. Recordings, museum demonstrations, reconstructed performances, film and television scores, theatre software, sample libraries, electronic controllers and website databases all give distant and past sounds a chance to be met again.
這趟旅圖沒有一口氣把世界攤開。隔壁家像真的過了一天。: This journey does not spread the whole world out in one go. The house next door lives through a day, as if for real.
遠方讓人知道聲音有來處，手邊讓人知道聲音會發生在身體附近。兩邊一起走，耳朵才會慢: Distance shows us that sound comes from somewhere; what is at hand shows us that sound happens close to the body. Walk with both, and the ears will slowly wake up.
那天早上，白兔先從地毯邊緣走過，腳步小到像怕吵醒什麼。刺蝟戴著圓眼鏡，忽然抬頭，: That morning the white rabbit crossed the edge of the rug first, steps so small it seemed afraid of waking something. The hedgehog, in round glasses, suddenly looked up, as if it had heard a very short, very exact signal arrive right on time. The capybara stayed where it was, slowly waiting for the cup's ring to die away. The chinchilla curled into a soft corner and made the whole room a little quieter.
隔壁女孩把一本厚厚的筆記本打開。裡面夾著照片、地圖、車票、樂器草圖，還有幾張她昨: The girl next door opened a thick notebook. Inside were photographs, maps, tickets, sketches of instruments, and a few pages of notes she had read the night before until she forgot to sleep.
隔壁家就從這些入口出發。看形狀，也聽材料；查來源，也試手感；走向遠方，也把聲音帶: The house next door sets out from these entrances. Look at the shape, and listen to the material. Check where it comes from, and try how it feels. Go far away, and bring the sound back into daily life.
隔壁家的世界聲音旅圖，常常不是從機場開始。: The Sound Journey of the house next door does not usually begin at an airport.
隔壁家的世界聲音旅圖：從古老樂器到現代耳朵的聲音巡禮 — 循著聲音，走進不同文化: The Sound Journey of the house next door: from ancient instruments to the modern ear — follow the sound into the places where different cultures make it.
隔壁男孩沒有立刻看名字。他先戴上耳機，閉起眼睛。長音慢慢走出來，像從很遠的地方經: The boy next door did not look at the name right away. He put the headphones on and closed his eyes. A long tone came out slowly, as if it had travelled from far away, passed through his chest and drifted out of the window. The low end went down to the soles of his feet, a drum pushed his shoulder, and when the bow hair crossed the string, that sound like a person about to speak made him rewind the track.
